title: Elon Musk’s gas strategy shows how the US market is changing | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Ed Crooks argues SpaceX's pipeline and liquefaction build-out for Starship LNG is small in volume but illustrates a shift in US gas from supply-push to demand-pull, with LNG and power customers securing dedicated supply. The newsletter also covers Hormuz shipping attacks, Brent near $110, Microsoft's withdrawal from an English data centre over grid delays, and a softened EU combustion-engine ban.

insights.claim: Each Starship launch uses about 1,000 tons of LNG, around 48 million cubic feet of gas, so even SpaceX's requested maximum of 456 launches a year would be about 60 mmcf/day, only about 0.07% of US gas consumption.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Starship is immaterial to gas balances today; the signal is in sourcing strategy.
insights.quote: Each launch uses about 1,000 tons of LNG, which is about 48 million cubic feet (mmcf) of gas.

insights.claim: If Musk's goal of 30 launches a day were realised, Starship would account for about 1.7% of US gas consumption and use about 11 million tons per year of LNG, comparable to the output of some large Gulf coast plants.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Only at the aspirational cadence does rocket fuel become a market-moving gas buyer.
insights.quote: At that rate of activity, Starship would account for about 1.7% of US gas consumption.

insights.claim: SpaceX has filed to build an eight-mile Starpipe pipeline linking a new liquefaction plant at Starbase to the Bay Runner pipeline, plus a 32-mile connection from the Florida Gas Transmission system to Cape Canaveral, and is recruiting a gas trader.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Vertical integration into pipelines, liquefaction and trading shows SpaceX treating energy as a critical supply-chain input.
insights.quote: The company has filed for approvals to build an eight-mile gas pipeline called Starpipe

insights.claim: Starship's progress includes entering orbit and deploying a payload for the first time last month, and Crooks says its size and reusability could cut the cost of delivering objects into orbit by orders of magnitude.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Launch-cost deflation underpins the long-run space economy that would drive fuel demand.
insights.quote: could reduce the cost of delivering objects into orbit by orders of magnitude
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning Because of its size

insights.claim: Crooks judges that Musk is keeping up with where the gas sector is going rather than ahead of it, unlike his pioneering role in electric vehicles and batteries.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: SpaceX's gas moves follow, rather than lead, a market trend already under way.
insights.quote: he is keeping up with where the sector is going, not ahead of it

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie argues North American gas has moved from two decades of abundance and supply-push pipeline investment, where producers sought new markets, to a market where customers actively secure supply.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Contracting power shifts toward buyers who lock in dedicated supply, changing how midstream is financed.
insights.quote: Pipeline investment reflected supply-push goals, as producers tried to open up new markets for their gas

insights.claim: Dedicated supply at discounted prices and year-round firm capacity have become top priorities for LNG producers and power generators, who now fund infrastructure that end users historically avoided because of uncertainty over long-term gas demand.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: End-user-funded pipelines reduce developer risk and favour projects tied to LNG and power demand.
insights.quote: having access to dedicated supply with discounted prices and year-round firm capacity have become top priorities

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's analysis of US pipeline capacity added over 2025-31 finds the majority is driven by LNG plants or power generators needing supply.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: New pipeline build is demand-anchored, not speculative.
insights.quote: the majority is being driven either by LNG plants or by power generators needing supplies

insights.claim: US gas demand is surging for LNG exports and power generation even as production hits record highs, and the market is set to tighten over the next few years, motivating deals such as Japanese buyers' acquisitions of US gas production.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Hedging and securing upstream supply is a rational response to expected tightening.
insights.quote: securing supplies and hedging price exposure in a market that is set to tighten over the next few years

insights.claim: Microsoft withdrew from a planned GBP 2 billion AI data centre with Nscale in Loughton, Essex after UK Power Networks warned it could not provide an adequate grid connection until the early to mid-2030s.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Grid connection delays are now a binding constraint that can cancel AI data centre projects in the UK.
insights.quote: Microsoft has withdrawn from a plan to build a new AI data centre in England

insights.claim: Brent crude rose close to US$110 a barrel in the week before publication, its highest since May, as Iran claimed hits on two VLCCs and the UKMTO recorded 11 other attacks on Gulf shipping in a week.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Gulf shipping risk is feeding directly into oil prices; the VLCC incidents were Iranian claims without UKMTO confirmation.
insights.quote: Brent crude rose close to US$110 a barrel last week, its highest level since May.
insights.locator: Iran claims hits on two VLCCs

insights.claim: Germany's Chancellor Merz and France's President Macron agreed to relax EU car-industry climate rules, easing the sale of internal combustion cars after 2035, under pressure from surging Chinese EV sales.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Europe is softening its combustion-engine phase-out, with competitive pressure from China cited as a driver.
insights.quote: The ban on combustion engines is now history.

insights.claim: US energy storage installations hit another record in Q2 2026 by megawatt hours, with longer-duration storage growing rapidly on solar and wind penetration, falling battery costs, data centre growth and policy incentives.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Storage demand is broadening and lengthening in duration, supported by data centre load.
insights.quote: installations hit another record in Q2 2026, in terms of megawatt hours of capacity
